brief: Prepare a 180–260-word English status note for a fictional island visitor desk as of 15 February 2026. Based only on S1 and S2, explain whether a new ferry can be advertised as available from 1 March, distinguish superseded plans from current commitments, and specify what must be verified before accepting bookings. Cite source IDs; avoid treating proposed dates or trial permission as a confirmed passenger service.

sources.text: Fictional operator notices. 1 February 2026: the operator proposed launching passenger service on 1 March, contingent on vessel delivery and operating permission. 10 February 2026: delivery slipped; the operator withdrew the 1 March target and proposed 15 April as the earliest possible passenger launch, subject to delivery, trials and final operating permission. No tickets had been released as of that notice.

Fictional port status log, last updated 14 February 2026. A 12 February entry allows non-passenger trial sailings during March; it does not authorize carrying paying passengers. The vessel had not been delivered by the update. There is no final passenger-service permission, confirmed timetable or booking release. The log makes no prediction about when those items will be completed.

reports.A:
## Visitor Desk Status Note — 15 February 2026

**Ferry Service Update: Do Not Advertise 1 March Availability**

The 1 March passenger service launch **cannot be advertised**. This date was **superseded** on 10 February when the operator withdrew it due to delayed vessel delivery and proposed **15 April as the earliest possible launch**, still contingent on delivery, trials, and final operating permission (S1). No tickets have been released.

**Current commitments versus proposed plans**

| Aspect | Status |
|--------|--------|
| 1 March passenger service | **Withdrawn** — superseded by 10 February notice (S1) |
| 15 April passenger launch | **Proposed only** — not a firm commitment (S1) |
| March sailings | **Trial permission only** — non-passenger, no paying customers permitted (S2) |

**Critical distinction:** The 12 February trial sailing permission for March explicitly excludes paying passengers and does not constitute passenger-service authorization (S2).

**Verification required before accepting any bookings**

1. **Vessel delivery** — not completed as of 14 February (S2)
2. **Successful trials** — pending; trial permission alone is insufficient (S1, S2)
3. **Final operating permission for passenger service** — not issued (S2)
4. **Confirmed timetable and booking release** — none exists (S2)

**Recommendation:** Continue advising visitors that no ferry bookings are possible. Monitor for operator and port authority updates on delivery completion, trial outcomes, and final passenger-service authorization.

reports.B:
## Island Visitor Desk Status Note — 15 February 2026

**Ferry Service Update**

The visitor desk **cannot advertise a new ferry as available from 1 March 2026**.

**Superseded plans versus current commitments**

The operator's initial proposal for a 1 March passenger launch has been withdrawn. Per S1, this target was contingent on vessel delivery and operating permission; following a delivery slip, the operator proposed 15 April as the earliest possible passenger launch. No tickets were released at that time. The 1 March date is therefore **superseded**; only the 15 April proposal remains as a current operator target, and this remains **provisional**.

**Current status per port authority**

S2 confirms that a 12 February entry permits only **non-passenger trial sailings during March**; this does not authorize carrying paying passengers. The vessel had not been delivered as of 14 February. No final passenger-service permission, confirmed timetable, or booking release exists.

**What must be verified before accepting bookings**

Before any bookings can be accepted, the following must be confirmed: (1) **vessel delivery**; (2) **successful completion of trials**; (3) **final operating permission for passenger service**; and (4) **official release of tickets and timetable** (S1, S2). Trial permission alone does not constitute a confirmed passenger service.
